Title: AGT-18 — Search Logs Source Attribution + Unified Search Latency View
Description:
**Phase 1 · P1 follow-up · Persona: Patricia (ops)**

### Goal

Make Patricia's latency view cover **both** agent searches and fast-path searches **without** mixing fast-paths into `ai_runs`.

### Context (verified during [SAN-589](https://linear.app/sanjiovani/issue/SAN-589/agt-00c-mastra-telemetry-and-ai-tracing))

* PR #90 / [SAN-589](https://linear.app/sanjiovani/issue/SAN-589/agt-00c-mastra-telemetry-and-ai-tracing) **(AGT-00C)** adds `ai_runs.metadata.tool_spans` for **true agent turns** only.
* Verification showed **fast-path routes already write latency into** `search_logs` through the shared search functions (`searchRentals()`/`searchEvents()`/`searchRestaurants()` → `writeSearchLog`). Both the agent tool and the fast-path REST route call the same shared fn, so fast-path latency **is** captured.
* **The gap is attribution/reporting:** `search_logs` lacks a `source`/caller dimension, and Patricia's view only reads `ai_runs` (which misses fast-paths).

### Scope

1. **Add** `source` **column to** `search_logs` (migration):
   * `source: 'agent' | 'fast-path'`
   * default `'agent'` (or `'unknown'` for old rows if safer).
2. **Update** `SearchLogPayload` (`src/mastra/lib/search-logs.ts`): add `source` field → insert it.
3. **Update call sites:**
   * agent tools pass `source: 'agent'`
   * `/api/rentals/search` passes `source: 'fast-path'`
   * `/api/events/search` passes `source: 'fast-path'`
   * `/api/restaurants/search` passes `source: 'fast-path'`
   * any grounded search fast-path passes `source: 'fast-path'`
4. **Patricia ops query/view:**
   * `search_logs` = universal per-search latency (now attributable by `source`)
   * `ai_runs.metadata.tool_spans` = per-agent-turn rollup
   * dashboard/report reads **both** (union), not one.

### Acceptance criteria

* `search_logs` rows include `source`.
* A fast-path search row records `source = 'fast-path'`.
* An agent search row records `source = 'agent'`.
* **No fake** `ai_runs` **rows are created for fast-paths.**
* **PR #90 scope remains unchanged.**
* Migration included and tested (column add on existing RLS'd table — no new table).
* Localhost proof shows both sources (one fast-path query + one agent query → two `search_logs` rows with distinct `source`).

### Dependencies

**Blocked by** [SAN-589](https://linear.app/sanjiovani/issue/SAN-589/agt-00c-mastra-telemetry-and-ai-tracing) **(AGT-00C).** Adjacent to DATA-041 / SEARCH-003 ranking-quality observability — the `source` dimension feeds that view too.

### Effort

0.5d.

Title: AGT-04A — Grounding-assertion output processor
Description:
**Phase 1 · P1 · Persona: ALL**

### Business value

The scorers (AGT-00A/B) **measure** hallucination offline/sampled; this processor **enforces** it in real time. A custom output processor that rejects/flags any reply citing a listing/event/venue ID not present in that turn's tool results — turning the concierge's "tool results are the only truth" clause from a prompt hope into a runtime contract. Highest user-facing safety win in Phase 1.

> Split from old AGT-04: 04A (this, custom logic + tests) vs 04B (SystemPromptScrubber, config) vs 04C (PIIDetector, config).

### Technical implementation

* **API (verified):** extend `BaseProcessor` (present in `@mastra/core` processors) with a `processOutputResult` hook; register in concierge `outputProcessors`. Runs **server-side on tool results before** `TOOL_CALL_RESULT` **is emitted** to AG-UI — so it can validate card payloads even though the v1 bridge is thin.
* Compare entity/ID references in the reply against IDs present in that turn's tool results (reuse the AGT-00A/00B grounding logic + AGT-03 schema).
* **Generative-UI paths (audit correction):** cards are rendered from **tool state**, not just prose — validate the **structured card payload**, not only the assistant's text.

### Flow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[Agent draft reply + card payload] --> B[Grounding-assertion processor]
    B --> C{Every card/ID present in tool results}
    C -- yes --> D[Pass untouched]
    C -- no --> E{Strictness}
    E -- flag --> F[Log and annotate]
    E -- block --> G[Strip fabricated card/ref]
    D --> H[User]
    F --> H
    G --> H
```

### Acceptance criteria

* A reply referencing a fabricated listing/event ID is blocked or flagged.
* **Card-payload validation covers all four kinds — Rental · Event · Restaurant · Venue (grounded)** — each card checked against that turn's tool results, not just prose citations. A fabricated card of any kind with no matching tool row is caught.
* A fully-grounded reply + cards pass untouched. Decisions logged + visible in traces (AGT-00C).

### Test requirements

* Vitest: fabricated-ID reply blocked/flagged; grounded reply passes — **one fixture per card kind (rental/event/restaurant/venue)**.
* Playwright: forced fabricated card → processor blocks/replaces (dev flag).

### Dependencies

**Blocked by AGT-00A + AGT-00B** (shares grounding logic) + **AGT-03** (schema). Pairs with the scorers as the enforce-half.

### Effort

1d (generative-UI handling is the design cost).
Creator: ai@socialmediaville.ca

Title: AGT-01 — Native tool-approval (host publish + checkout)
Description:
**Phase 1 · P1 (demoted from P0) · Persona: Roberto, Andrés**

### Business value

Roberto's publish and Andrés' payment are irreversible. Today the only gate is the React `renderAndWaitForResponse` HITL — the **agent/tool layer has no server-side pause**. A bug or a non-CopilotKit caller skips the gate. Native `requireApproval` enforces the pause server-side.

> **Demoted P0→P1 (correct):** host publish already has working CopilotKit HITL; checkout doesn't exist in Mastra yet.

### ⚠️ Spec correction 1 (audit — verified)

`preview_and_publish` **is a CopilotKit** `useCopilotAction` **(**`host-event-copilot-bridge.tsx:106-118`**,** `renderAndWaitForResponse`**), NOT a Mastra** `createTool`.

### ⚠️ Spec correction 2 (CopilotKit-v1 verified 2026-06-06 — THIS CHANGES THE APPROACH)

`@ag-ui/mastra@0.2.1-beta.2` **does NOT forward Mastra** `tool-call-approval` **to CopilotKit.** Probed its dist: emitted AG-UI events = `RUN_STARTED · STATE_SNAPSHOT · TEXT_MESSAGE · TOOL_CALL(_ARGS/_END/_RESULT)`; `approval` **= 0 hits.** So Mastra-native `requireApproval` **cannot drive the v1 UI** — the approve/decline event will never reach the React layer through the bridge.

**→ On Phase 1 (CK v1), option (a) "migrate to a Mastra tool with** `requireApproval` **and surface approval chunks to the UI" is NOT viable. Use option (b) DUAL-LAYER:**

* **UI approval stays** `renderAndWaitForResponse` (the existing CK action) — this is the only path that renders on v1.
* **Mastra** `requireApproval` **is a SERVER-SIDE enforcement gate** on the underlying publish/mutation tool, resolved by the action's commit route (`/api/approval-commit`), so a non-React caller still hits a hard pause.
* Driving the approval **UI** from native `requireApproval` (AG-UI approval chunks) is a **v2/Phase-2** capability — do not spec it for v1.

Touch points: `host-event-copilot-bridge.tsx`, `event-publish-approval-panel.tsx`, `host-event-prompt.ts`, `/api/approval-commit`.

### Acceptance criteria

* A declined approval does **not** mutate — proven **at the server/tool layer without the UI** (API test), not just in React.
* Approved path completes and logs `approved`/`declined` to `ai_runs`.
* v1: UI pause via `renderAndWaitForResponse`; server pause via Mastra `requireApproval` — both proven.

### Test requirements

* Vitest: server-side `requireApproval` suspend→resume + suspend→decline at the tool layer (no UI).
* Vitest: `/api/approval-commit` schema (auth-first). Playwright: declined approval → no DB mutation. Localhost proof.

### Dependencies

Host-publish: dual-layer above. Checkout half: blocked on **AGT-11 (**[SAN-601](https://linear.app/sanjiovani/issue/SAN-601/agt-11-checkout-workflow-mastra-deterministic-idempotent-hitl)**)** + **PAY-001 (**[SAN-178](https://linear.app/sanjiovani/issue/SAN-178/pay-001-live-ticket-purchase-on-production)**)**. AG-UI approval-event UX → revisit after CK **v2** migration.

### Effort

1d (host publish, dual-layer).

Title: AGT-06 — ResponseCache + CostGuardProcessor
Description:
**Phase 1 · P1 · Persona: Camila (latency), Sofía (cost)**

### Business value

Directly attacks the two LESSONS.md cost/latency findings: identical repeat queries (common on `/`) skip the LLM round-trip (latency win for Camila), and `CostGuardProcessor` is a runaway-spend circuit breaker per resource/window (cost insurance even at low MVP scale).

### Technical implementation

* **API (verified):** `ResponseCache` + `CostGuardProcessor` present in `@mastra/core/processors`.
* Add `ResponseCache` to concierge (TTL + `resourceId`/tenant scope).
* **Cache key (audit correction):** key on **intent + normalized query + neighborhood**, NOT the raw string — Camila refines "under $80" → "$75" and "1BR Laureles" should still hit. A raw-string key would miss every refinement.
* Add `CostGuardProcessor` (per-resource spend cap per window); **document thresholds as Infisical env vars**.
* Log cache hits to `ai_runs.metadata`.
* **Measure via AGT-00C first** — cache-hit rate is invisible without traces.

### Acceptance criteria

* Second semantically-equivalent request hits cache (no model call observed in trace).
* A refined query that maps to the same intent+neighborhood still hits (not a raw-string miss).
* CostGuard blocks once the per-resource cap is exceeded.

### Test requirements

* Vitest: cache hit on equivalent input (no model invocation); refinement hit; CostGuard trips past cap.

### Dependencies

Best measured after **AGT-00C** (tracing).

### Effort

0.5d.
Creator: ai@socialmediaville.ca

Title: AGT-03 — Structured Output for evaluationAgent / scorer judge
Description:
**Phase 1 · P1 · Persona: All (scorer plumbing)**

### Business value

`evaluationAgent` emits unvalidated "JSON-style" text by prompt instruction — fragile, can break the reranker silently. `structuredOutput` guarantees a typed, validated `.object`. **The same Zod schema is reused by the AGT-00A/00B scorer judge**, so this is foundational plumbing, not cosmetic.

### Technical implementation

* Define a Zod rerank/verdict schema (shared with scorers).
* Call with `structuredOutput: { schema, errorStrategy: 'warn' }`.
* **Gemini caveat (verified in plan):** tools + structured output don't always coexist → set `jsonPromptInjection: true`; optionally offload to a secondary judge `model`.

### Acceptance criteria

* `evaluationAgent` returns a validated `.object`.
* Invalid model output triggers the `warn`/fallback path — never throws to the user.

### Test requirements

* Vitest: malformed model output → fallback (no throw); valid output → typed object.

### Dependencies

Supports **AGT-00A** / **AGT-00B** (shared schema). No blockers.

### Effort

0.5d.

Title: CONCIERGE-001 — CoAgentsProvider + AvailableAgents enum for multi-domain consumer routing
Description:
## Goal

Add a `CoAgentsProvider` wrapper and `AvailableAgents` enum to centralize multi-agent React state, mirroring the pattern from `examples/showcases/multi-agent-canvas`.

Pure infrastructure refactor — no new agents, no new UI. Reorganizes how existing agents (`conciergeAgent`, `rentalAgent`, `eventAgent`, etc.) are wired into consumer pages so any component can read agent state without prop-drilling.

---

## Why

Currently each page calling `useCoAgent` inlines a string literal for the agent name. As the consumer chat routes across domains (rentals, events, venues, restaurants), agent state fragments across components. `CoAgentsProvider` gives a single React context and replaces magic strings with a typed enum.

---

## Scope

### `AvailableAgents` enum

```typescript
// src/lib/agents/available-agents.ts
export enum AvailableAgents {
  CONCIERGE = "conciergeAgent",
  RENTAL = "rentalAgent",
  EVENT = "eventAgent",
  HOST_EVENT = "hostEventAgent",
  ROUTER = "routerAgent",
}
```

All `useCoAgent({ name: "..." })` string literals replaced with `AvailableAgents.*`.

### `CoAgentsProvider`

```typescript
// src/components/copilot/coagents-provider.tsx
export const CoAgentsProvider = ({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) => {
  const { state: conciergeState } = useCoAgent<MdeState>({
    name: AvailableAgents.CONCIERGE,
    initialState: defaultMdeState,
  });
  const { state: rentalState } = useCoAgent<RentalAgentState>({
    name: AvailableAgents.RENTAL,
    initialState: defaultRentalState,
  });

  return (
    <AgentsContext.Provider value={{ conciergeState, rentalState }}>
      {children}
    </AgentsContext.Provider>
  );
};

export const useAgentsContext = () => useContext(AgentsContext);
```

### Mount point

Inside `CopilotKitProvider` in `src/components/copilot/copilot-kit-provider.tsx`:

```tsx
<CopilotKit runtimeUrl="/api/copilotkit" agent={AvailableAgents.CONCIERGE}>
  <CoAgentsProvider>
    {children}
  </CoAgentsProvider>
</CopilotKit>
```

### Migration

* `src/app/page.tsx` — remove inline `useCoAgent`, consume via `useAgentsContext()`
* `src/app/rentals/page.tsx` — same
* `src/components/host/host-event-copilot-bridge.tsx` — use `AvailableAgents.HOST_EVENT`

---

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `AvailableAgents` enum created; zero raw string literals remain in `useCoAgent` calls
- [ ] `CoAgentsProvider` mounts without TS errors
- [ ] `useAgentsContext()` works in `/` and `/rentals` consumer pages
- [ ] No regressions: `npm run dev` boots, concierge chat still responds
- [ ] Vitest: context shape test + renders children

---

## References

* Source pattern: `examples/showcases/multi-agent-canvas/frontend/src/components/coagents-provider.tsx`
* CopilotKit **v1 only** — `useCoAgent` from `@copilotkit/react-core` at `1.55.2`. No v2 imports.

---

## Out of Scope

* `running` status badge → CONCIERGE-002
* New agents or agent capabilities

Title: CRM-012 — Partner settings, account management + background workflow infrastructure
Description:
## Goal

Complete the Phase 1 Partner CRM foundation with:

1. Partner settings + account management page (`/partner/settings`)
2. Partner hub index routing (`/partner` → dashboard or onboarding)
3. Background workflow infrastructure (cron endpoint + follow-up scheduler)

No AI, no CopilotKit, no Gemini. Pure server-side logic.

---

## Scope

### `/partner` root page

* Server component that checks `partner_profiles.onboarding_complete`
* If `false` → redirect to `/partner/onboarding`
* If `true` → redirect to `/partner/dashboard`
* Handles unauthenticated → redirect to `/login?next=/partner`

### `/partner/settings` page

**Account section**

* Display name, contact email, phone (editable)
* `PATCH /api/partner/settings/account`

**Notification preferences**

* Toggles per notification type: `new_lead`, `booking_request`, `booking_update`, `follow_up_reminder`
* Stored in `partner_profiles.notification_prefs` (jsonb column — add via migration)
* `PATCH /api/partner/settings/notifications`

**Pricing defaults**

* Minimum booking hours, deposit percentage, cancellation window (days)
* Stored in `partner_profiles.pricing_defaults` (jsonb column — add via migration)
* `PATCH /api/partner/settings/pricing`

**Danger zone**

* "Deactivate account" → sets `partner_profiles.is_active = false`, signs out
* `POST /api/partner/settings/deactivate` — requires `reason` string
* No hard delete in Phase 1

### API routes (all server-only, F13 carve-out applies)

| Route | Method | Auth |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `/api/partner/settings/account` | PATCH | partner session |
| `/api/partner/settings/notifications` | PATCH | partner session |
| `/api/partner/settings/pricing` | PATCH | partner session |
| `/api/partner/settings/deactivate` | POST | partner session |
| `/api/cron/follow-up-check` | GET | `CRON_SECRET` header |

### Cron endpoint — `/api/cron/follow-up-check`

Runs on a schedule (daily at 9am COT). Finds leads where:

* `status = 'new'` AND `created_at < NOW() - INTERVAL '24 hours'`
* No existing `partner_notifications` row with `type = 'follow_up_reminder'` for the same `lead_id`

Creates `partner_notifications` rows + logs to `partner_activity_log` with `action = 'follow_up_reminder_sent'`.

Auth: validates `Authorization: Bearer ${CRON_SECRET}` header — reject with 401 if missing or wrong.

```typescript
// /api/cron/follow-up-check/route.ts (server-only, service-role allowed per F13)
export async function GET(req: NextRequest) {
  const secret = req.headers.get('authorization')?.replace('Bearer ', '');
  if (secret !== process.env.CRON_SECRET) return new Response('Unauthorized', { status: 401 });
  // ... query + insert notifications
}
```

Vercel Cron config in `vercel.json`:

```json
{
  "crons": [{ "path": "/api/cron/follow-up-check", "schedule": "0 14 * * *" }]
}
```

(14:00 UTC = 09:00 COT)

### Supabase migration additions

```sql
-- Add columns to partner_profiles
ALTER TABLE partner_profiles
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS notification_prefs jsonb DEFAULT '{
    "new_lead": true,
    "booking_request": true,
    "booking_update": true,
    "follow_up_reminder": true
  }'::jsonb,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS pricing_defaults jsonb DEFAULT '{
    "min_booking_hours": 3,
    "deposit_pct": 30,
    "cancellation_window_days": 7
  }'::jsonb,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS is_active boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT true;

-- Index for cron query
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_partner_leads_cron
  ON partner_leads(partner_id, status, created_at)
  WHERE status = 'new';
```

RLS: `notification_prefs` and `pricing_defaults` inherit existing `partner_profiles` policies. `is_active = false` partners cannot log in — add check in auth middleware.

---

## UI Components

* `PartnerSettingsLayout` — left nav tabs: Account · Notifications · Pricing · Danger Zone
* `AccountSettingsForm` — react-hook-form + zod, optimistic updates
* `NotificationPrefsForm` — toggle switches per notification type
* `PricingDefaultsForm` — number inputs with validation
* `DeactivateAccountModal` — confirmation dialog with reason textarea

All forms: save button shows "Saving…" state, toast on success/error. No AI, no CopilotKit.

---

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `/partner` correctly routes to onboarding vs dashboard based on `onboarding_complete`
- [ ] `/partner/settings` loads with all three settings sections
- [ ] Account PATCH updates DB and shows success toast
- [ ] Notification toggles persist across page reload
- [ ] Pricing defaults saved and used as prefill in booking forms (CRM-007)
- [ ] Deactivate flow sets `is_active = false` and signs out
- [ ] `/api/cron/follow-up-check` rejects without correct `CRON_SECRET`
- [ ] Cron creates `partner_notifications` for stale leads (tested via direct API call)
- [ ] Vitest: all API route handlers covered
- [ ] `npm run dev` boots clean, all routes return expected status codes

---

## Dependencies

* Blocked by: CRM-001 (schema), CRM-010 (notifications table)
* Related: CRM-006 (leads — cron targets `partner_leads`), CRM-007 (bookings — uses pricing defaults)

---

## Out of Scope (Phase 2)

* Email/SMS delivery of follow-up reminders
* AI-generated follow-up message suggestions (SAN-804)
* White-label subdomain settings

Title: AGT-17 — Golden query evaluation suite
Description:
**Phase 1 (tail) · P2 · Persona: Lucía (QA), Patricia (ops)**

### Business value

Scorers (AGT-00A/00B) are only trustworthy against a **fixed, repeatable benchmark**. Without a golden set, "faithfulness 92%" is a number with no denominator. This is the regression gate that proves the scorers work and catches quality drift before Camila/Tourist see it. **Not a launch blocker**, but it's what makes 590/605 believable.

> **Reuse, don't duplicate:** **DATA-006 (**[SAN-336](https://linear.app/sanjiovani/issue/SAN-336/data-006-golden-eval-queries-cafe-restaurant-nightclub)**)** "Golden eval queries" already shipped for venues. AGT-17 extends that dataset + wires it to the new Mastra scorers — do **not** create a parallel corpus.

### Technical implementation

* Curate a golden query set (build on DATA-006):
  * **20 rental** — e.g. *"2BR Laureles under 3M"*
  * **20 venue / grounded** (café + nightlife) — e.g. *"quiet rooftop dinner in Provenza"*
  * **20 restaurant** — e.g. *"best bandeja paisa near Parque Lleras"*
  * **10 event** — e.g. *"salsa this weekend"*
* Run each through the concierge → score with AGT-00A (faithfulness) + AGT-00B (grounding) → emit a CI report.
* Wire `.claude/skills/mastra/evals/evals.json` into the run (the file AGT-00A converts).

### Acceptance criteria

* 70-query suite runs in CI (sampled on prod, full in CI) and emits a pass/fail report.
* **Thresholds:** faithfulness ≥90, grounding coverage ≥90; a trace attached per scored query.
* A deliberately fabricated-result fixture **fails** the suite (proves the gate bites).

### Test requirements

* Vitest/CI: suite runs green on current prod behavior; red on injected hallucination fixture.

### Dependencies

**Blocked by AGT-00A (**[SAN-590](https://linear.app/sanjiovani/issue/SAN-590/agt-00a-hallucination-faithfulness-scorer)**) + AGT-00B (**[SAN-605](https://linear.app/sanjiovani/issue/SAN-605/agt-00b-grounding-coverage-scorer)**)** — needs the scorers. Builds on **DATA-006 (**[SAN-336](https://linear.app/sanjiovani/issue/SAN-336/data-006-golden-eval-queries-cafe-restaurant-nightclub)**)**.

### Effort

1d.

## Summary

Create the final Trips release gate. This proves the MVP runs locally, passes tests, survives production smoke checks, and has enough evidence for Sofía to call it ship-ready instead of just implemented.

## User journey

Camila can open Trips in the deployed app → create/use a trip → see saved items, itinerary, map, conflicts, booking-backed items, mobile layout, and recovery behavior → Patricia and Sofía can verify logs and smoke evidence if something breaks.

## Frontend work

* Smoke `/trips`, saved collections, trip workspace, itinerary, map, conflict HITL, add-to-trip, and mobile viewports.
* Confirm loading/error/empty states are production-safe.
* Verify no console errors on critical Trips surfaces.
* Capture production or preview screenshots/evidence as required by repo task lifecycle rules.

## Backend / Supabase work

* Run production-safe smoke checks for Trips tables, RLS, sync paths, reconciliation, cache hydration, lifecycle state, and observability logs.
* Confirm no service-role key leaks to client bundles.
* Verify Stripe-related paths with safe test-mode or mock evidence, not live accidental charges.
* Check indexes/RPCs/policies required by Trips are present in the target environment.

## Agent / CopilotKit / Mastra work

* Smoke CopilotKit/Mastra connection on Trips-relevant actions and HITL cards.
* Confirm Gemini is read-only for booking/payment/trip truth and cannot fabricate persisted state.
* Verify agent traces/logs exist for Trips tools where implemented.
* Keep model-dependent checks focused on connectivity and guardrails, not exact prose.

## Tech stack

Next.js 16, React 19, Tailwind 4, shadcn/ui, CopilotKit 1.55.2, Mastra, Gemini, Supabase, Google Maps, Places API, Stripe where relevant, Playwright.

## Dependencies

* Internal: TRIP-011, TRIP-013, TRIP-015, TRIP-016, TRIP-017, TRIP-018

## Acceptance criteria

* Trips MVP passes local floor gates and production/preview smoke checks.
* Evidence includes commands, URLs, screenshots/traces, and any known limitations.
* RLS, sync, reconciliation, cache, mobile, observability, lifecycle, and retry coverage are accounted for.
* Any production blocker is recorded and the issue stays open until resolved.
* No task is marked Done without the required runtime proof unless it is pure-doc and marked N/A.

Title: AGT-00B — Grounding-coverage Scorer
Description:
**Phase 0 · P0 · Persona: ALL**

### Business value

Where AGT-00A (faithfulness) asks "did the reply invent anything?", the grounding scorer asks the complementary question: "is **every** claim in the reply backed by a tool result?" Together they enforce the concierge's "tool results are the only truth" contract from both directions (no fabrication + full coverage).

> **Critical note — these two scorers share one judge + one schema.** AGT-00B is built as a **thin extension** of AGT-00A (same Gemini judge, same AGT-03 verdict schema, second assertion), NOT a separate pipeline. Effort reflects that. The two audits list "hallucination / grounding" as **one** P0 — we split into A (build) + B (extend) only to keep acceptance criteria crisp; ship them in the same cycle.

Title: AGT-00A — Hallucination / Faithfulness Scorer
Description:
**Phase 0 · P0 · Persona: ALL (Camila, Tourist, Andrés, Roberto)**

### Business value

**The single biggest production-quality gap.** We ship AI search with **0 scorers** (`/api/scorers` → 404). Nothing catches an invented rental, restaurant, venue, event, price, or booking detail before a user sees it. The concierge prompt *declares* "tool results are the only truth"; **nothing measures it.** Largest production-quality gap in both audits.

### Technical implementation

* **API (verified 2026-06-05):** use `createScorer` **/** `MastraScorer` **from** `@mastra/core` (declared in `dist/evals/base.d.ts`). The standalone `@mastra/evals` **package is NOT installed** — do not import it.
* Add a scorer (not an agent — `evaluationAgent` is mislabeled) that, given (tool outputs, final reply), detects entities/prices/IDs in the reply absent from tool output.
* Judge model = Gemini (reuse `evaluationAgent`'s model as the judge); structured verdict via AGT-03 schema.
* Convert `.claude/skills/mastra/evals/evals.json` (exists, unwired) into a runtime scorer registration.
* Run sampled/async on prod turns (logged to `ai_runs.metadata`), full on the golden-query suite in CI.

### Flow

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[Concierge turn] --> B[Tool outputs]
    A --> C[Final reply]
    B --> D[Scorer createScorer]
    C --> D
    D --> E{Reply entity in tool output}
    E -- no --> F[Unfaithful low score]
    E -- yes --> G[Faithful pass]
    F --> H[Log ai_runs.metadata]
    G --> H
```

### Acceptance criteria

* `/api/scorers` lists the hallucination scorer.
* A reply citing a fabricated listing/event/price scores as unfaithful; a fully grounded reply passes.
* Scores recorded per scored turn; golden-query suite reports a faithfulness rate.

**Phase 0 · P1 severity / do-now (trivial) · Persona: Sofía (hygiene), all (defense-in-depth)**

### Business value

`getLocalAgentsWithLogging` iterates `mastra.listAgents()` **unconditionally** (`src/mastra/copilotkit/logging-mastra-agent.ts:83` — verified). All 7 registered agents are exposed on the CopilotKit runtime; the UI only ever pins `conciergeAgent` + `hostEventAgent`. Any client holding the runtime URL could invoke `routerAgent` — which the frozen `MASTRA-MIS-001` decision lists as an explicit anti-pattern. **Latent, not active** (the `agent=` prop pins selection), but it's a \~15-min fix that aligns the runtime with the frozen routing doc.

> Audit nuance: june5 audit **downgraded this P0→P1** because the prop pins selection. Kept in Phase 0 only because it is trivially cheap, not because severity is P0.

### Technical implementation

* Allowlist exposed agents to `["conciergeAgent", "hostEventAgent", "pingAgent"]` in `logging-mastra-agent.ts` (filter `listAgents()` keys).
* **Optional housekeeping (same PR):** quarantine `conciergeRoutingWorkflow` (registered against its own MIS-001 "do not wire" rule); flag `rentalAgent`/`eventAgent` as prune candidates (strict subsets of concierge). Pruning the agents can defer — the allowlist already makes them unreachable.

### Acceptance criteria

* Runtime exposes only the 3 allowlisted agents; `routerAgent`/`rentalAgent`/`eventAgent`/`evaluationAgent` not invocable via `/api/copilotkit`.
* Concierge + host wizard unaffected (regression check).

### Test requirements

* Vitest: allowlist filter returns exactly the 3 keys.
* Localhost proof: concierge + host turns still work.

### Dependencies

None.

### Effort

0.25d.
